newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK jobs, sales, earnings data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK jobs, sales, earnings data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists's reactions to data showing UK November retail sales up 0.7 pct m/m and 3.9 pct y/y, November unemployment down 95,800 at 6.9 percent and October average earnings up 4.0 percent:
"Very large fall indeed in unemployment, retail sales also above consensus. Very strong data which will certainly increase pressure on the chancellor to increase rates."

"It was said that the introduction of the jobseekers' allowance would make the series very volatile and I think that is somewhat of an understatement...The one possible good thing if you are the chancellor hoping not to raise rates is that the rise in unit wage costs was slightly lower. Negative for both the short and long end of the UK yield curve."

"Clearly there are some distortions involved in this (unemployment). But I suppose the bottom line is that the underlying decline is much better than expected. The overall picture is one of an economy which perhaps is performing much more akin to what the Bank of England is thinking at the moment than the Treasury wants to see. To that extent, I think the Chancellor will really miss the boat if he doesn't raise interest rates at the next monetary meeting in January."

"The data are clearly stronger than expected and that's what's going to grab the markets attention. This does suggest problems mounting for the future. When you take out the special effects they're citing, you're still looking at a fall of 70,000 in unemployment and that's evidence of a very significant tightening in the labour market. As yet it's not really showing through in the wage and cost data so I don't think it's an immediate problem for inflation."

"Eddie George will be arguing on the back of this that some tightening is needed and it's going to be hard for Ken Clarke to defend his position. I think he may well do that -- he will look at retail sales and see that the year on year growth rate has come down a little bit -- but I still think they are strong data and will worry the gilt market."

"The retail sales confirm that the surveys perhaps under-estimated the strength of sales in November. The underlying trend looks strong throughout and it now looks like December should break back above the 4.0 percent level. There is no negative response to the higher prices we have been seeing. Demand is strengthening and is going to continue to do so into the new year, keeping the pressure on for higher base rates."

"The fall of almost 96,000 in unemployment is hard to acccept at face value...I don't think this fully reflects the underlying conditions in the labour market. Average earnings haven't risen, unit wage costs have been revised down across the board. The retail sales are possibly of more concern to the market as they confirm that consumption is going to be a big driving force for the economy next year. The data make an interest rate increase more likely in January or February but I still think Clarke may try to get through until the election."

"The data just mean that the upward presssures on base rates are not going to abate in the near future, general elections notwithstanding. I think we may not get the pre-Christmas boom in sales that some retailers are expecting. At the end of the day the economy is probably growing above trend and is likely to for several more quarters at least, so it needs to be slowed down."
